findings.title: Tenant isolation is application-only; no database-enforced row-level security
file_line_evidence: backend/app/database.py:20-24 — lab_id held in contextvars.ContextVar, not a DB session setting
backend/app/database.py:284-298 — get_db() yields a plain Session; no SET LOCAL / current_setting / tenant role
backend/migrations/versions/*.py (all 107 files) — zero CREATE POLICY / ROW LEVEL SECURITY / current_setting() statements (grep verified)
findings.reproduction: Static: `grep -rniE 'ROW LEVEL SECURITY|CREATE POLICY|current_setting\(|SET LOCAL' backend/migrations/versions/*.py` returns zero DDL policy hits. Falsification: point to any migration that creates an RLS policy or to get_db() setting a tenant context — none exists.
findings.root_cause: Multi-tenancy was implemented exclusively as `lab_id == actor.lab_id` filters in repository/service queries; no database-level defense in depth.
findings.impact: A single omitted/incorrect lab_id predicate in any query (present or future) exposes cross-tenant PHI. No DB-level backstop; national deployment raises breach and confidentiality impact.
findings.recommended_remediation: Owner decision first (ADR-A/tenant architecture): evaluate PostgreSQL RLS with session tenant context as defense in depth; meanwhile run a static query audit asserting every PHI-table query carries a lab_id predicate.
alternatives: (1) Keep app-only scoping + mandatory query-lint gate (lowest cost, weaker)
(2) Add RLS policies per tenant-bearing table (strong, migration-heavy, owner-gated)
(3) Separate schemas/databases per tenant (strongest, highest TCO, conflicts with national single-deployment model)

findings.title: Unguarded drop_constraint in 20260815_0016 breaks fresh-install and drifted-DB upgrade paths
file_line_evidence: backend/migrations/versions/20260815_0016_device_tenant_isolation.py:16-21 — op.drop_constraint('uq_integrated_devices_uid', ...) with no table/constraint existence guard
backend/migrations/versions/20260815_0016_device_tenant_isolation.py:22-26 — creates composite (lab_id, device_uid) unique constraint
backend/migrations/versions/20260815_0016_device_tenant_isolation.py:29-39 — downgrade re-adds global unique on device_uid
findings.reproduction: Static: construct a database where uq_integrated_devices_uid does not exist (fresh install whose ORM model already declares only the composite constraint) and run `alembic upgrade 20260815_0016`; the unguarded drop raises a lookup error. Falsification: show a runtime inspector guard in upgrade(). Contrast guarded sibling backend/migrations/versions/20260815_0002_scope_inbox_idempotency.py:27-40. Downgrade falsification: insert two rows with same device_uid under different lab_id, then downgrade — global unique creation fails.
findings.root_cause: Migration authored for one lineage state only; no inspector-based idempotency guard unlike neighbouring revisions.
findings.impact: Forward upgrade can abort mid-chain on fresh/drifted databases; downgrade is data-dependent and may fail after legitimate per-lab duplicate UIDs exist.
findings.recommended_remediation: Wrap both drop and create in inspector guards (mirroring 20260815_0002) and document a data-reconciliation precondition for downgrade.
alternatives: (1) Guard with inspector (recommended, mechanical)
(2) Move constraint changes into a new forward-only reconciliation migration behind ADR-A
(3) Accept forward-only and make downgrade a documented no-op with explicit warning

findings.title: Claims global idempotency uniqueness and NOT NULL constraints dropped; downgrade not reliably reversible
file_line_evidence: backend/migrations/versions/20261114_0001_unify_foundation.py:9-11 — header claims 'Every statement is additive or widening ... safe on an existing database'

backend/migrations/versions/20261114_0001_unify_foundation.py:106-120 — op.execute('ALTER TABLE claims DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS claims_idempotency_key_key') then composite unique index (lab_id, idempotency_key)
backend/migrations/versions/20261114_0001_unify_foundation.py:83 and :97 — _drop_not_null('organizations','name'), _drop_not_null('facilities','name')
backend/migrations/versions/20261114_0001_unify_foundation.py:172-176 — downgrade re-adds global UNIQUE (idempotency_key)
findings.reproduction: Static: read lines 106-120 and compare with the header claim at 9-11. Falsification attempt: two claims rows with identical idempotency_key in different labs after upgrade; downgrade then fails re-adding global unique. Also note downgrade deliberately does not restore NOT NULL (line 178-180).
findings.root_cause: Idempotency scope was changed from global to per-lab, but the migration is documented as purely additive and its downgrade assumes pre-change data uniqueness.
findings.impact: Data-integrity semantics silently weakened; documentation misstates the operation class (breaking, not additive); partial rollback can fail on production data, contradicting recorded rollback posture.
findings.recommended_remediation: Correct the header to 'breaking (constraint scope change)'; record the idempotency-scope decision with the owner; provide a documented data check before downgrade or make downgrade conditional and honest about residual state.
alternatives: (1) Forward-only with documented residual state (recommended)
(2) Data-reconciliation downgrade that deduplicates keys (destructive — requires owner approval)
(3) Revert the scope change (would undo MP/ODR-scoped per-lab design — owner-gated)

findings.title: Forward migration performs unlogged data deletion (role-permission over-grant repair)
file_line_evidence: backend/migrations/versions/20260814_0006_security_audit_governance.py:179-184 — DELETE FROM niam_role_permissions WHERE role='organization_manager' AND permission='audit.read'
findings.reproduction: Static read of upgrade() lines 179-184. Falsification: show an audit row written for this deletion or a downgrade step restoring the grant — neither exists in the file.
findings.root_cause: Security over-grant repair implemented as inline DML in an Alembic upgrade with no accompanying audit event or reversal path.
findings.impact: Authorization state changes without an immutable audit trail; if the repair is later deemed wrong, no deterministic restoration path. Low likelihood of harm because the deletion is narrowly scoped.
findings.recommended_remediation: Emit a structured audit event for authorization-state DML in migrations and document the intended final grant set; avoid relying on migration DML as the sole control record.

findings.title: Every OAuth2-issued access token is rejected by the platform's own protected endpoints
file_line_evidence: backend/app/security/oauth2_provider.py:119-128 — create_access_token_oauth2() sets payload['type'] = 'oauth2_access'
backend/app/security/auth.py:99-106 — decode_token() returns None unless payload['type'] == 'access'
backend/app/security/dependencies.py:37-50,71-75 — get_current_user() uses decode_token() and rejects None; requires user_id
backend/app/security/oauth2_provider.py:151-158 — decode_oauth2_token() is the only decoder accepting 'oauth2_access'
grep — decode_oauth2_token has ZERO call sites anywhere in backend/app (definition only)
backend/app/routes/oauth2.py:144-160 — /oauth2/token issues these unusable tokens
findings.reproduction: Static data-flow: /token -> create_access_token_oauth2(type='oauth2_access') -> presented as Bearer to any protected route -> get_current_user -> decode_token -> type mismatch -> None -> 401. Falsification: show a route/dependency that calls decode_oauth2_token, or change create_access_token_oauth2 to type='access' and add user_id for client_credentials. Neither exists.
findings.root_cause: OAuth2 provider was built as a parallel token kind with its own (orphaned) decoder instead of integrating with the canonical decode_token/get_current_user chain.
findings.impact: The entire OAuth2/OIDC authorization-code and refresh-token flow is non-functional against GULA's own API — tokens can be minted but never used. Any relying party integrating against advertised OAuth2 endpoints fails at first call. Public discovery advertises these endpoints as usable.
findings.recommended_remediation: Owner decision on OAuth2's role; then either (a) unify token type with canonical 'access' and populate user_id/lab_id/perm_ver claims, or (b) wire decode_oauth2_token into an accepted dependency and define its authorization semantics. Add an end-to-end test that mints via /token and calls a protected route.
alternatives: (1) Unify into canonical token pipeline (recommended; single decoder)
(2) Keep separate decoder + explicit OAuth2 dependency on selected routers
(3) Mark OAuth2 NOT INTEGRATED and remove from discovery until owner rules

findings.title: OAuth client registration and scope/grant assignment are ungoverned; grant_types never enforced
file_line_evidence: backend/app/routes/oauth2.py:54-80 — POST /oauth2/register requires only get_current_user (no admin permission); caller chooses allowed_scopes, grant_types, response_types, token_endpoint_auth_method
backend/app/routes/oauth2.py:83-141 — /authorize stores caller-supplied `scope` verbatim (line 127); no check against client.allowed_scopes
backend/app/routes/oauth2.py:144-160 — /token dispatches on data.grant_type without checking client.grant_types
backend/app/routes/oauth2.py:242-249 — token_endpoint_auth_method == 'none' skips client secret verification
backend/app/security/oauth2_provider.py:212-216 — discovery advertises auth method 'none' and scopes openid/profile/email/read/write
findings.reproduction: Static: any authenticated user can POST /register with is_confidential=false, token_endpoint_auth_method='none', allowed_scopes=['system:admin'], grant_types=['client_credentials']; then /authorize accepts an arbitrary scope. Falsification: show a permission dependency on /register or a scope/grant allowlist check at token issuance — absent in cited lines. Present impact is bounded because get_current_user requires user_id (client_credentials tokens have none) and RBAC reads roles, not token scope; but any scope-consuming relying party would be exposed.
findings.root_cause: Client onboarding treated as self-service utility; no governance boundary around OAuth2 trust anchors.
findings.impact: Attacker-controlled scope claims in minted tokens; public clients with arbitrary grants; governance/NIST least-privilege gap. Present platform RBAC limits escalation, so impact is latent rather than confirmed.
findings.recommended_remediation: Require an admin/governance permission for client registration; validate requested scope against allowed_scopes at /authorize; enforce grant_types and response_types at /token and /authorize; restrict 'none' auth method to explicitly approved public clients.
alternatives: (1) Govern registration + enforce all allowlists (recommended)
(2) Disable OAuth2 registration/issuance until owner rules (safe, matches current non-functional state)
(3) Keep permissive with monitoring (not recommended for national platform)

findings.title: JWT validation enforces only exp/iat — no audience, issuer or subject binding
file_line_evidence: shared/auth/jwt.py:18-25 — _validate_claims() registry has exp and iat only
shared/auth/jwt.py:60-72 — decode_access_token() calls _validate_claims; no aud/iss checks
backend/app/security/oauth2_provider.py:119-129 — access-token payload has jti/client_id/type/user_id/scope but no aud or iss
backend/app/security/auth.py:99-106 — decode_token() adds only a type check
findings.reproduction: Static: read the JWTClaimsRegistry construction at shared/auth/jwt.py:19-22 — keys are exp and iat. Falsification: show aud/iss in the registry or in create_access_token_oauth2 payload — absent.
findings.root_cause: Token validation was designed for a single shared-secret audience; no multi-client/national relying-party model was implemented.
findings.impact: Tokens minted for one client/realm are accepted anywhere the shared HMAC key is known; no audience isolation between national services. Contributes to OIDC claim-conformance gap.
findings.recommended_remediation: Add aud/iss to issued tokens and validate them against configured expected values in decode_access_token; coordinate with AUD-API-002 unification so one decoder enforces the full claim set.
alternatives: (1) Full claims validation (recommended)
(2) Document single-audience limitation and keep HOLD (current posture)
(3) Separate signing keys per audience (higher key-management cost; ODR-gated asymmetric decision pending)

findings.title: OAuth2 introspection and revocation endpoints require no client authentication
file_line_evidence: backend/app/routes/oauth2.py:163-188 — POST /oauth2/introspect: no Depends on client auth; returns active, client_id, user_id, scope, token_type, exp
backend/app/routes/oauth2.py:191-205 — POST /oauth2/revoke: no client authentication; any caller can mark a token revoked
backend/app/security/oauth2_provider.py:205-210 — discovery advertises both endpoints
findings.reproduction: Static: both function signatures contain only data/request/db parameters — no _authenticate_client call (contrast /token at line 150). Falsification: show a client-auth dependency or _authenticate_client() call inside introspect/revoke — absent.
findings.root_cause: RFC 7662/RFC 7009 client-authentication requirements were not implemented; endpoints were added as simple token-hash lookups.
findings.impact: Token information disclosure to any holder of a token string, and unauthenticated denial-of-service via revocation. Global IP rate limit exists but is a coarse mitigation, not client authentication.
findings.recommended_remediation: Require client authentication on both endpoints and restrict introspection response fields to those the authenticated client is entitled to (RFC 7662 §2.2).
alternatives: (1) Client auth + field scoping (recommended)
(2) Remove endpoints from discovery and disable until implemented
(3) Keep as-is relying on global rate limit (not recommended)

findings.title: Active FHIR R4 router accepts arbitrary unvalidated JSON and returns non-FHIR errors
file_line_evidence: backend/app/factory.py:656-658 — capabilities.fhir_interoperability.routes is MOUNTED (unlike the non-activated T6 router)
backend/app/capabilities/fhir_interoperability/schemas.py:21-22 — FHIRResourceInput model_config = ConfigDict(extra='allow')
backend/app/capabilities/fhir_interoperability/service.py:56,67 — payload.model_dump(exclude_none=True) persisted verbatim into FHIRResourceRecord.resource
backend/app/capabilities/fhir_interoperability/routes.py:26-31,107-112,155-156 — errors are plain HTTPException(detail=str), not application/fhir+json OperationOutcome
backend/app/capabilities/fhir_interoperability/schemas.py:79-86 — CapabilityStatement declares fhirVersion 4.0.1 but no type/profile/terminology validation
findings.reproduction: Static: POST /fhir-interoperability/resources with a valid resourceType plus arbitrary extra fields; schemas.py:22 allows them and service.py:56 stores them. Trigger 404 at routes.py:155-156 and observe a plain `{"detail": ...}` body, which is not an R4 OperationOutcome. Falsification: point to a canonicalization/allowlist step or an OperationOutcome exception handler on this router — neither exists. (The non-activated T6 router does implement OperationOutcome, but is not mounted.)
findings.root_cause: The mounted capability is a thin persistence facade; FHIR conformance is represented by type names and a CapabilityStatement rather than by validation of FHIR structures, references, profiles or terminology.
findings.impact: Stored PHI resources may contain arbitrary client-controlled fields; interoperability clients cannot rely on FHIR error semantics; nominal R4 conformance could be mistaken for real conformance in national integration.
findings.recommended_remediation: Set extra='forbid' (or canonicalize through the in-repo Health Core FhirR4Adapter), validate CodeableBinding/terminology and references, and add an exception handler emitting R4 OperationOutcome for all failures on this router.
alternatives: (1) Reuse canonical FHIR adapters + OperationOutcome (recommended; reuse before build)
(2) Keep facade but document as NOT FHIR-conformant and remove R4 claims from CapabilityStatement
(3) Activate T6 router instead after real auth boundary (owner-gated, D-020)

findings.title: HL7 OBX numeric values 'NaN'/'Infinity' cause HTTP 500 in active FHIR conversion endpoint
file_line_evidence: backend/app/capabilities/fhir_interoperability/hl7.py:96-107 — float(value) with no isfinite() guard; NaN/Infinity flow into valueQuantity.value
backend/app/capabilities/fhir_interoperability/routes.py:71-85 — POST /hl7/convert returns the bundle dict via FastAPI JSON serialization
Starlette JSONResponse.render (verified from installed source) — json.dumps(..., allow_nan=False)
findings.reproduction: Static: send an ORU^R01 message whose OBX-5 is 'NaN' (or 'Infinity'); _observation_value returns float('nan'); Starlette JSONResponse raises ValueError on allow_nan=False → 500. Falsification: show math.isfinite() guard or string coercion before serialization — absent.
findings.root_cause: Numeric parsing accepts all float() lexical forms without domain validation; response serialization is strict RFC 8259.
findings.impact: Low-cost unauthenticated-to-this-router (but system:admin at router level) request can produce 500s and log noise; corrupt numeric FHIR observations if a non-strict serializer is later introduced.
findings.recommended_remediation: Reject non-finite floats (math.isfinite) and emit valueString or a 422 for non-numeric/non-finite OBX values; bound OBX-5 length.
alternatives: (1) isfinite guard (recommended)
(2) Coerce to string (loses numeric semantics)
(3) Pydantic strict Decimal parsing

findings.title: Terminology/DICOM 'support' is declaration-only — hardcoded lists with no validation engine
file_line_evidence: backend/app/integration/standards/terminology.py:31-42 — supported systems from a hardcoded string map with zero concepts

backend/app/integration/standards/terminology.py:50-54 — validate() delegates to an empty CodeSystem for known systems (always False unless concepts registered); fallback branch unreachable for supported systems
backend/app/integration/standards/terminology.py:69 — is_supported() returns True purely from the string map
backend/app/integration/standards/dicom.py:37-61 — DICOMService has dataclasses and service/modality name lists, no DIMSE/network/UID validation
backend/app/integration/standards/fhir.py:32-35 — validate() checks only presence of 'resourceType'

backend/app/health_core/terminology/validators.py:225-303 — real LOINC check-digit/ICD-10/UCUM allowlist validators exist here, but WS-E guard keeps this package out of factory/main (backend/tests/health_core/test_quality_review_static.py:120-130)
findings.reproduction: Static: instantiate TerminologyService; get_system('LOINC') creates an empty CodeSystem (lines 34-39); validate('LOINC','718-7') then evaluates `'718-7' in {}` -> False, while is_supported('LOINC') -> True. No DICOM protocol module exists in app/integration/standards/dicom.py. Falsification: show a caller that registers curated concepts into the active TerminologyService or a real DICOM engine — grep shows none.
findings.root_cause: Standards support was modeled as capability descriptors for reporting, not as validation engines; the robust validators live in an intentionally non-wired synthetic slice.
findings.impact: LOINC/SNOMED/ICD-10/UCUM and DICOM support claims in /integration/standards and NATIONAL_SERVICE_CONTRACTS are not enforceable in the active runtime; downstream clinical data can carry unvalidated codes/units.
findings.recommended_remediation: Either wire the curated Health Core validators into the active boundary (respecting WS-E — do NOT move HTTP code into health_core) or explicitly reclassify standards support as NOT IMPLEMENTED in contracts. Add code-system content before claiming validation.
alternatives: (1) Reuse canonical validators via an adapter outside health_core (recommended)
(2) Relabel descriptors as 'declared, not validated' and keep HOLD
(3) Build new validators (violates reuse-before-build)

GOVERNANCE/PHASE_B_EVIDENCE/PHASEB_T6_FHIR_EVIDENCE.md:84-88,132-134,160-163 — X-GULA-Principal header is synthetic; spoofable if activated
backend/app/factory.py — no fhir_http import/reference (verified by grep); only capabilities.fhir_interoperability is mounted at :656-658

backend/tests/health_core/test_quality_review_static.py:30,407,410-418 — WS-E guard: FINAL_DECISION.md MD5 effdfeaf10234678d83b2668c4489552 (verified matching on disk) and no HTTP/DDL artifacts in health_core; guard holds
findings.reproduction: Static: grep 'fhir_http' in factory.py/main.py -> no hits; md5sum GOVERNANCE/FINAL_DECISION.md -> matches guard constant; AST guard conditions read and satisfied. Falsification: show a factory include_router for fhir_http (none) or a modified guard constant/MD5 mismatch (none). No defect is active today — this is a residual activation gate recorded for completeness.
findings.root_cause: Interim design uses a test-only header principal pending a real identity/authz boundary (D-020 owner-gated).
findings.impact: Currently zero runtime exposure. If mounted before replacing the synthetic principal, any caller able to set headers can impersonate a tenant/facility principal and access FHIR resources.
findings.recommended_remediation: Keep non-activated (MP-001/ODR posture respected). Add a CI guard asserting no fhir_http import in factory/main, and require a real signed-token boundary plus D-020 ruling before activation.
alternatives: (1) Keep dormant + CI guard (recommended)
(2) Replace header principal with canonical auth then activate (owner-gated, D-020)
(3) Delete the router (destroys strategic dormant asset — not permitted)
